title: Follow-up: readBlobs must fail indeterminate on a missing or ambiguous object
description: Round-2 review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#38, new finding 1 (rated highest of the round-2 findings). src/git.ts:139-145 treats a cat-file --batch header of '<oid> missing' or '<oid> ambiguous' as a skip; snapshotAtRef then drops every entry whose text is undefined. On a corrupt object store, or a partial (--filter=blob:none) clone whose promisor remote is unreachable, a blob the tree lists is silently left out of the --ref index: the file is never walked, unresolvedSites is not incremented, and the command exits 0 with a short answer -- in exactly the mode whose promise is that an empty answer is never read as 'no impact'. It persists too: program.ts keys the cache from the ls-tree listing alone, so the incomplete index is written and later served under the full-tree key. The comment at git.ts:142-144 already states the intended behaviour ('an indeterminate repository, not a miss'); the code does not. Fix: throw indeterminateError from readBlobs (or return the missing ids and have snapshotAtRef throw), and add a test that fabricates a 'missing' header. No healthy repository reaches this, which is why it is MINOR, but it is the one place in the new code where a wrong answer is silent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cat-file --batch header of `<oid> missing` or `<oid> ambiguous` makes readBlobs throw an indeterminate error; a `--ref` impact run over such a tree exits 7 with stdout empty.
A unit test fabricates a batch response containing a `missing` header and drives that path without a corrupt repository; it goes red if the `continue` is restored.
A failed `--ref` build writes no cache entry, so a short index cannot later be served under the full-tree key.
A healthy tree is unchanged: the existing ref tests stay green and `bun run check` passes.

plan: Make readBlobs throw indeterminateError on any missing or ambiguous header instead of continuing; keep the truncated-header and truncated-body checks as they are.
Add a unit test with a fabricated batch response that contains a missing header, asserting the indeterminate error_type and exit code 7.
Add a test that a failed --ref build writes no cache entry, so a short index cannot be served later under the full-tree key.
Prove the healthy path unchanged: the existing ref tests stay green and bun run check passes.
